facts.value: The table maps cyclic sound indices 0, 1, 2, and 3 to bit patterns 3, 2, 0, and 1 respectively: FGM and BGM on, FGM on with BGM off, both off, and FGM off with BGM on. Because an accepted chord advances the index before applying it, repeated inputs move from the initial normal state through music off, music and sound effects off, sound effects off, and back to normal; the overlay uses the same mapping to keep its status label synchronized. The labels reflect the local selected bits, not a readback of effective audio gains. Setup resets indices without calling the audio-mode setter, so repeated setup can desynchronize labels and stored mixer enables until another chord applies them.
facts.rationale: Correct inherited claim using pinned source and recorded object observations.

facts.value: The sound-output index cycles modulo 4 and the information-display index cycles modulo 8 on each accepted X plus D-pad-left chord. Display states 0–3 hide the panel and states 4–7 show it. For each sampled voice statistic, a new high value replaces the retained value and starts a 240-update countdown; the countdown decreases during visible updates, after which the retained value follows the current sample and the countdown is clamped to zero. The countdown is decremented on the same call that sets it to 240, leaving 239. Hidden modes with an existing panel freeze peaks and timers; a missing panel seeds both values and zeroes timers on every call. The inspected db_RunEveryFrame caller invokes CheckSoundInfo for all four players, and each invokes UpdateSoundInfo, producing four updater calls per caller pass.
facts.rationale: Correct inherited claim using pinned source and recorded object observations.

facts.value: Mode changes are restricted to player 0 and require a chord with one constituent newly pressed while the other remains held. Each accepted chord advances the four-state sound index and eight-state display index exactly once. The audio configuration is reapplied only if the sound index changed, while display updating occurs unconditionally, including calls for other player indices. Button masks are observed, not consumed. The once-per-chord property assumes one player-0 call per newly computed pressed mask; repeated calls with the same edge can advance again. The inspected caller does make one call for each player index per pass, but all four calls update diagnostics.
facts.rationale: Correct inherited claim using pinned source and recorded object observations.
